incremental.claim: a positive delta means the index carries information the comparison model does not; it does NOT establish a distinct mechanism

hierarchical.note: configurations resampled in the outer loop, pilot paths in the inner loop, so the interval carries the uncertainty of estimating the index itself

matched_simple.reading: positive means the member of a pair with the LOWER index did better, which is the direction the index predicts once volatility and observation noise are held close

matched_index.reading: the index is a SUFFICIENT summary only if matched pairs perform alike. A mean absolute difference comparable to the spread of the outcome says it is not, however well it predicts on average

settings.index_note: R = median over regimes of (observations needed to determine the sign of the advantage) / (informative observations available). Defined in heiner_abm.learnability.learnability_ratio and imported unchanged; this module never redefines it.

covariates.adv_noise: |mean advantage| / s.d. of the observed gain, from pilot paths
covariates.log_regime_len: log10 of the expected regime length (1 / hazard)
covariates.avail: share of periods whose demand is observed
covariates.delay: periods between a demand occurring and its observation
covariates.log_memory_window: log10 of the learner's effective window (1 + lambda) / (1 - lambda)
covariates.log_evidence: log10 of informative observations per regime, from pilot paths
covariates.default_gap: mean |default order - oracle order|, from pilot paths

V1.claim: The index adds predictive accuracy beyond the prespecified comparison model, on held-out configurations.
V1.decision_rule: Supported if the lower limit of the bootstrap interval on the added cross-validated R-squared exceeds 0. Supports: the index is a USEFUL SUMMARY INDEX carrying information the listed quantities do not. Does NOT support: a distinct mechanism.

V2.claim: The index still adds accuracy on process families it was not fitted on.
V2.decision_rule: As V1, fitting on the jump family and scoring on switch and drift. Failure here with V1 supported means the index summarizes within a process but does not transfer.

V3.claim: The added accuracy survives the uncertainty of estimating the index from pilot paths.
V3.decision_rule: As V1, with pilot paths resampled inside each configuration resample. A V1 supported and V3 not means the apparent gain is within the noise of measuring the index.

D1.claim: Holding simple uncertainty measures close, configurations with a lower index do better.
D1.decision_rule: Matched pairs close in standardized log sigma and log(1 + tau) and far apart in the index. Supported if the interval on the mean within-pair difference lies above 0.

D2.claim: Holding the index close, the underlying process does not matter.
D2.decision_rule: Matched cross-family pairs close in the index. The index is a SUFFICIENT summary only if the mean absolute within-pair difference is small relative to the spread of the outcome. This claim is reported, never asserted: a large difference is evidence against sufficiency, not against usefulness.
